name: Cessna Citation III/VI/VII (650)
summary: The first swept-wing, T-tail Citations, a long-range 1980s family still flown widely by charter and corporate operators.

engines: Two Garrett/Honeywell TFE731 turbofans in pods on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Long, slim fuselage with a row of small windows
tail: T-tail with a swept fin and swept horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Swept wing and T-tail but plain wingtips with no winglets
Slim, long body with a long row of small windows
Rear pods on a Citation-style airframe

confusedWith.howToTell: The Citation II has a straight wing and a low-set tailplane; the Citation III/VII has a swept wing and a T-tail.
The Sovereign has larger oval windows and (on the Sovereign+) winglets; the III/VII has smaller, rounder windows and plain tips.
The Learjet 55/60 has small winglets and a sharper needle nose; the Citation III/VII has plain wingtips and a more rounded nose.
The Hawker 800 has a cruciform tail with the stabilizer partway up the fin; the Citation III/VII has a true T-tail.
